tips.title: Generation and editing tips
items: Choose one readable action. Specify the supporting foot, hand positions and camera angle when the pose matters.
Try one change per request, such as a lower camera, warmer light or a different expression, so the comparison stays useful.
For a campaign scene, describe the sign or wall carrying the exact text and keep the message short.
For reference edits, assign each image a role and separate what stays from what changes.
Keep the full silhouette inside the frame and leave room for a later camera move. Inspect faces, hands, feet and text before saving.

prompts.title: City skate — KEEP GOING
prompts.prompt: A vibrant cinematic live-action sports-campaign still, 16:9 widescreen. A fictional female skateboarder around twenty-six, wearing a burnt-orange windbreaker, loose navy trousers and simple cream sneakers, is captured at the clean apex of a small controlled ollie over a low curb on a sunny Lisbon street. Her whole body and the complete skateboard are visible, both feet positioned convincingly above the deck, natural hands balancing the movement, focused face clearly visible. Use a low three-quarter camera angle and a believable body pose rather than an extreme stunt. Two adult friends react naturally on the sidewalk behind her, with a cafe terrace and a real city street receding into the distance. A large painted wall advertisement on the left reads exactly "KEEP GOING" in two crisp, oversized dark-blue lines on a pale warm-yellow background; the lettering is physically painted on the wall and follows its perspective. Late afternoon sunlight creates long diagonal shadows, tactile stucco and real skin texture. Crisp subject with a small amount of natural motion blur in the moving background, 28mm cinema lens, rich but controlled colors, energetic editorial composition with real depth. Keep the skateboarder away from the frame edges. A candid decisive moment from a premium commercial film, one cohesive image with no added title, collage or border.

prompts.title: Station dance — NEXT STOP ANYWHERE
prompts.prompt: An arresting live-action cinematic still, 16:9 widescreen. In a grand early-twentieth-century European railway concourse, a fictional adult dancer in their late twenties, dressed in a flowing cobalt-blue overshirt, ivory T-shirt, charcoal trousers and worn white sneakers, is caught mid-turn during an impromptu dance. The full body is visible with a convincing grounded pivot, one foot on the stone floor, natural arms extended at different heights, relaxed readable hands and a face lit by a shaft of late-afternoon sun. Several adult commuters continue walking in the deeper background, some glancing toward the dancer. Tall windows, iron arches and a large station clock create a rich architectural backdrop. A physically installed departure-board-style sign in the middle background reads exactly "NEXT STOP" on its first line and "ANYWHERE" on its second line, in clean cream block lettering on a deep-blue panel. Clothing has a light natural motion blur at its edges while the face and torso remain sharp. Warm sun against cool interior shadow, long floor reflections, atmospheric depth, 35mm cinema lens, restrained grain, beautiful believable skin and fabric. Frame the scene like the opening of a moving human story with space for a slow dolly-in, not a studio dance portrait. One coherent realistic location, no floating lettering or graphic overlay.

faqs.q: When should I choose Seedream 5.0 Flash?
faqs.a: Flash is the fast variant of the Seedream 5.0 family. Use it for visual exploration: test a character pose, framing or campaign direction through individual image requests.

faqs.q: Can Flash return several variations in one request?
faqs.a: Flash returns one generated image per request. Launch a new request for another variation, or choose Seedream 5.0 Lite for image sets.

faqs.q: Can I edit an existing character image?
faqs.a: Yes. Use up to 10 reference images, identify the face, outfit and framing to preserve, and describe the change. Review the resulting identity and details before keeping it.
Choose 1K, 1.5K or 2K and download JPEG or PNG. For a native transparent-background asset, choose Seedream 5.5.

faqs.q: Can a Flash image become the opening of a video?
faqs.a: Yes. Save the chosen still and use it as a reference in a compatible video model. Plan motion separately; Flash itself produces a still image.

faqs.q: How do I check the current price?
faqs.a: Choose your resolution and references in the image workspace. MaxVideoAI shows the quote before you confirm each request.

features.body: Describe a gesture that can be read in a single frame. Add a believable supporting pose, readable face and a setting with depth.

features.title: Try a different direction

features.title: Build a campaign around people

section.title: How to prompt Seedream 5.0 Flash
section.intro: Start with an action you can see in one instant. Add the body position, expression, camera angle and light, then describe the surroundings and any text.
section.tip: A plausible pose is more useful than an extreme stunt. Check hands, feet and props before using the image as a video reference.

globalPrinciples: Give the scene one action and a clear focal person.
For movement, describe the supporting foot, balance and readable hand positions.
Put exact words in quotation marks and place them on a physical surface.
Change one part of the brief per request so you can compare the direction.
